name: Semantic Redundancy Analysis
description: Analyzes the text for unnecessary semantic repetition, tautologies, and circular reasoning. Large Language Models often suffer from 'content looping'—where they restate the same core concept in different words to fulfill length constraints or because their attention mechanisms lose long-range narrative progression. This results in highly verbose, repetitive paragraphs that lack forward momentum.
algorithm: Semantic Density and Circular Concept Tracking
mechanism: The algorithm maps the conceptual propositions of each sentence into semantic embeddings. It then calculates the 'distance' or 'overlap' between propositions within the same paragraph or document. A human writer typically advances a narrative or argument with each sentence (high semantic progression). AI-generated text frequently produces sentences with 80-90% conceptual overlap with the preceding sentence, masked only by surface-level synonym swapping. The system also flags classic AI filler patterns like summarizing a point immediately after making it ('In summary...', 'Overall...').
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing essays, extended articles, and marketing copy where AI models are prompted to generate specific word counts, forcing them into repetitive padding.
strengths:
• Excellent at catching AI text that has been manually edited at the sentence level but retains its generative, repetitive structural flaws.
• Strongly correlates with the 'hallucination of length' phenomenon common in models like GPT-4 and Claude.
limitations:
• May flag human writing that is intentionally repetitive for rhetorical effect (e.g., political speeches) or poor-quality, 'fluff-filled' human writing.
• Less effective on very short texts where there simply isn't enough length for the AI to begin looping.
parameters:
Analysis: Sentence-level Semantic Entailment and Overlap
Metric: Propositional Progression Ratio
Output: 0-100 Semantic Redundancy (Looping) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-80% accuracy. Best used alongside Lexical Density and Argument Structure to differentiate between poor human writing and actual AI generation.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
Jawahar, G. et al. (2020). Automatic Detection of Machine Generated Text: A Critical Survey. COLING.
